data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental manual (DM) establishes procedures for the United States Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) enterprise information technology governance (EITG) framework and accompanying governance processes.
policy_statements.target: United States Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) enterprise information technology governance (EITG) framework and accompanying governance processes

policy_statements.source_text: USDA’s EITG framework is called the Integrated Information Technology Governance Framework (IITGF).
This DM provides an overview and implementation guidance for the USDA IITGF.
The Integrated Information Technology Governance Framework: Guidebook identifies the activities of each of the eight decision gates of the IITGF.
cross_references: Integrated Information Technology Governance Framework: Guidebook
policy_statements.target: activities of each of the eight decision gates of the IITGF

policy_statements.source_text: Decision gates are aligned with an investment’s lifecycle phase and enable USDA to manage its EITG processes.
This DM also defines the alignment activities and responsibilities of the Information Technology (IT) Executive Governance Board.
policy_statements.target: alignment activities and responsibilities of the Information Technology (IT) Executive Governance Board

policy_statements.source_text: These measures facilitate effective IT decision-making within USDA and include touchpoints with other governance, management, and control processes.

These include USDA’s IT Portfolio Management (ITPM) division, USDA’s System Development Lifecycle approach, project management, enterprise architecture (EA), the risk management framework, IT security and privacy controls, and Departmental Regulation (DR) 3575-004, Information Technology Security Baselines and Security Control Tailoring.
cross_references: Departmental Regulation (DR) 3575-004, Information Technology Security Baselines and Security Control Tailoring

policy_statements.source_text: Implementing an Integrated IT Governance Framework further supports the USDA mission by providing organizational alignment for decisions related to technology components, services, and applications.
This DM applies to all Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices with USDA major and non-major IT investments.
policy_statements.target: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices with USDA major and non-major IT investments

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA IITGF applies to all new and existing USDA major IT investments and projects.
policy_statements.target: new and existing USDA major IT investments and projects

policy_statements.source_text: This includes enhancements to existing major investments and projects associated with operations, maintenance, and disposition.
policy_statements.target: enhancements to existing major investments and projects associated with operations, maintenance, and disposition

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA IITGF also applies and should be leveraged during governance for any non-major investments at a Mission Area, agency, or staff office.
policy_statements.target: non-major investments at a Mission Area, agency, or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: This DM provides the procedures for the Departmental policy as outlined in DR 3130-010, United States Department of Agriculture Enterprise Information Technology Governance.
cross_references: DR 3130-010, United States Department of Agriculture Enterprise Information Technology Governance

policy_statements.source_text: This DM is supported by management oversight controls and processes.
It consists of:
The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996 (CCA), 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101, et seq.;
cross_references: The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996 (CCA), 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101, et seq.

policy_statements.source_text: This DM is effective immediately when published and will remain in effect until it is superseded or expires.

conditions: within six months of the date of publication

policy_statements.source_text: There are various legislative and regulatory drivers for implementing ITPM.
Many legal reforms emphasize the need for Federal agencies to significantly improve how they plan, select, fund, control, and evaluate IT initiatives.

The Federal approach to ITPM has been the select-control-evaluate model championed by OMB in OMB Circular A-11, Preparation, Submission, and Execution of the Budget; the Government Accountability Office (GAO); and industry experts since the early 1990s.
cross_references: OMB Circular A-11, Preparation, Submission, and Execution of the Budget

policy_statements.source_text: To give Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices guidance on implementing CCA and FITARA, OMB offers Circular A-130, Managing Information as a Strategic Resource.
cross_references: Circular A-130, Managing Information as a Strategic Resource

policy_statements.source_text: The Consolidated and Further Continuing Appropriations Act, 2015, P.L. 113-235, Division A, Title VII, Section 706 prohibits the use of funds to acquire new IT systems or significant upgrades without certain approval and concurrences.
cross_references: The Consolidated and Further Continuing Appropriations Act, 2015, P.L. 113-235, Division A, Title VII, Section 706
policy_statements.target: use of funds to acquire new IT systems or significant upgrades

policy_statements.source_text: These include the approval of the Chief Information Officer (CIO) and the concurrence of the Executive IT Investment Review Board (E-Board) and the Committees on Appropriations of both Houses of Congress.
IT governance involves collaborating to make strategic decisions about technology within an organization.
It connects business and IT leaders, ensuring alignment and adaptability in the ever-evolving IT landscape.
It covers four critical areas: strategic alignment, value delivery, risk management, and resource management.
The IITGF is a cohesive, streamlined governance structure that provides for executive-level decision-making.
It outlines the primary role that each governance board plays within the EITG process.
This ensures the accountability and success of governance objectives.
In the IITGF, governance boards and members represent the full complement of and formal authority over the business, financial, and IT organizations of USDA.
policy_statements.target: business, financial, and IT organizations of USDA

policy_statements.source_text: The IITGF is a comprehensive framework of policies and processes that ensures USDA’s formal, responsive, and effective oversight of IT resources.

It integrates enterprise and mission area governance, standardizes intake and review workflows, and aligns IT decision-making with USDA’s strategic priorities, compliance mandates, and operational needs.

This ensures operational efficiency and value delivery in the implementation of IT by enabling timely, evidence-based decisions; reducing duplication and rework through standardized artifacts; and ensuring that resources are directed toward initiatives with clear institutional fit, measurable impact, and sustained alignment with USDA’s mission.
The framework spans the entire IT lifecycle from initiation through disposition.
The Integrated Information Technology Governance Framework: Guidebook defines a series of eight governance decision gates and associated investment lifecycle phases.
cross_references: Integrated Information Technology Governance Framework: Guidebook

policy_statements.source_text: These promote effective executive oversight and management of IT investments.

An investment tailoring agreement (ITA) formalizes the requirements for requests to the Integrated Advisory Board (IAB) for customizing or waiving IITGF-specific phases, activities, decision gates, deliverables, or investment governance reviews.
These requests are based on specific investment requirements or business needs and can occur in any of the eight decision gates of the IITGF.
conditions: based on specific investment requirements or business needs

policy_statements.source_text: Personnel can use an ITA to request and obtain authorization.
They can also use an ITA to record the rationale for using, omitting, or integrating specific IITGF decision gate reviews.
An ITA determines the selection and granularity of deliverables for the investment or project.
It indicates the parameters of scope, schedule, budget, and quality, including any exceptions.
The Investment Manager or Project Manager (PM) for the investment must initiate and endorse the ITA.
After approval by a USDA IT governance board or its delegate, the ITA indicates permission for the project to advance.
conditions: After approval by a USDA IT governance board or its delegate

policy_statements.source_text: The procedure for each of the eight decision gates is the same, except for minor differences noted in the description of each decision gate.
conditions: except for minor differences noted in the description of each decision gate

policy_statements.source_text: Each investment or project is required to go through the following steps for each of the eight decision gates to meet IITGF requirements and obtain the necessary reviews and approvals from the required enterprise governance boards.
The Mission Area, Agency, or Staff Office Integrated Project Team (IPT):
Collaboratively identifies, addresses, and resolves issues (determines requirements);
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, or Staff Office Integrated Project Team (IPT)

policy_statements.source_text: Establishes project baselines and contract requirements; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, or Staff Office Integrated Project Team (IPT)

policy_statements.source_text: Provides required information to the Investment Manager or PM for developing the governance documentation package based on the decision gate.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, or Staff Office Integrated Project Team (IPT)

policy_statements.source_text: The Investment Manager or PM:
Reviews the completed decision gate approval documentation package; and
policy_statements.target: completed decision gate approval documentation package

policy_statements.source_text: Submits the approved documentation package to the Mission Area Agency, or Staff Office Investment Review Board (IRB).
The Mission Area, Agency, or Staff Office IRB:
Conducts an evaluation of the submitted materials; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, or Staff Office IRB

policy_statements.source_text: Decides whether to approve the governance request.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, or Staff Office IRB

policy_statements.source_text: If the governance request is approved, the IRB provides the required updates, action items, and conditions (if applicable) to the Investment Manager or PM.
policy_statements.target: required updates, action items, and conditions
conditions: If the governance request is approved
if applicable

policy_statements.source_text: If the governance request is not approved, the IRB notifies the Investment Manager or PM of the rejection and reason.
conditions: If the governance request is not approved

policy_statements.source_text: The Investment Manager or PM:
If the governance request was approved, the Investment Manager or PM sends the Decision gate documentation package to the Enterprise Governance Team Liaison prior to the deadline for their IAB.
conditions: If the governance request was approved
prior to the deadline for their IAB

policy_statements.source_text: If the governance request is not approved, the Investment Manager or PM updates the Decision gate documentation package and resubmits it to the Mission Area, Agency, or Staff Office IRB.
conditions: If the governance request is not approved

policy_statements.source_text: The Enterprise Governance Team Liaison:
Reviews the decision gate documentation package, supporting documentation, and IRB assessment for completion and accuracy; and
policy_statements.target: decision gate documentation package, supporting documentation, and IRB assessment

policy_statements.source_text: Notifies the E-Board and IAB of upcoming activities for this decision gate and routes materials and inputs to the E-Board and IAB for review and distribution to IAB and E-Board members in preparation for the meetings.
The E-Board and IAB:
Review the documentation submitted for the governance request; and
policy_statements.target: documentation submitted for the governance request

policy_statements.source_text: Decide whether to approve or disapprove it and provide decision memos signed by the appropriate board chair.
If the E-Board and IAB approve the decision gate documentation package, they send a signed approval memo, with any applicable action items or conditions, to the Mission Area Points of Contact (POC).
conditions: If the E-Board and IAB approve the decision gate documentation package

policy_statements.source_text: If the E-Board and IAB do not approve the decision gate documentation package, they send a signed disapproval memo, with applicable action items or conditions to be satisfied before resubmittal, to the Mission Area POCs.
conditions: If the E-Board and IAB do not approve the decision gate documentation package

policy_statements.source_text: Decision gate 1, personnel assess the need for a proposed investment.
They evaluate the alignment with Departmental, Mission Area, agency, or staff office strategic planning efforts.
policy_statements.target: alignment with Departmental, Mission Area, agency, or staff office strategic planning efforts

policy_statements.source_text: This decision gate allows Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices to develop the investment concept with preliminary business requirements, performance measures, benefits, and costs.
It allows the integrated IT governance boards to review these proposals and assess the impact and benefit to the overall IT portfolio.
Each newly proposed IT project or initiative proceeds through IITGF decision gate 1.
policy_statements.actor_name: newly proposed IT project or initiative

policy_statements.source_text: The IAB decides whether it is a major or non-major investment.
DR 3130-008, Definition of Major Information Technology Investments, defines major investments.
cross_references: DR 3130-008, Definition of Major Information Technology Investments

policy_statements.source_text: DR 3130-009, Non-Major Information Technology (IT) Investments, defines non-major investments.

If the new proposed IT project or initiative is a major IT investment or within a major investment it will follow the governance path in the Integrated Information Technology Governance Framework: Guidebook.
cross_references: Integrated Information Technology Governance Framework: Guidebook
policy_statements.actor_name: new proposed IT project or initiative
policy_statements.target: governance path in the Integrated Information Technology Governance Framework: Guidebook
conditions: If the new proposed IT project or initiative is a major IT investment or within a major investment

policy_statements.source_text: Review, recommendation, and decision authority at each level will vary based on the criteria and decision type per DR 3130-008.

If it is a non-major investment, the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Information Resource Management Center (IRMC) IT Strategic Planning and Governance (ITSPG) division will inform the Investment Manager or PM that the governance delegation will return to the Mission Area, agency, or staff office.
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Information Resource Management Center (IRMC) IT Strategic Planning and Governance (ITSPG) division
conditions: If it is a non-major investment

policy_statements.source_text: It will then proceed under that Mission Area, agency, or staff office governance structure.
Decision gate 2 ensures that the proposed or existing investment best supports the Department’s mission and objectives.
The investments are prioritized and evaluated for performance as measured by cost, schedule, performance, and risk, as well as technical alignment.
Decision gate 3 is required to determine the effectiveness, completion, and accuracy levels achieved throughout the investment’s planning activities.

This decision gate provides the integrated IT governance boards with information to further understand the strategy by which the proposed investment will achieve its scope, cost, and schedule objectives.
Decision gate 4 is for reviewing an investment’s functional requirements.
The functional requirements must be complete, unambiguous, and actionable enough to support detailed system design, acquisition planning, and downstream implementation.

This decision gate also allows the integrated IT governance boards to gain a complete understanding of the requirements and ensure that the requirements can support a detailed design of the proposed system.
Decision gate 5 ensures that any systems under review can proceed into system fabrication, development, and testing by conducting a formal design review.
This review compares the system’s final design against the stated performance requirements, cost, schedule, risk, and other constraints.
It does so by examining product specifications, engineering drawings, and configuration item documentation to confirm alignment with the product baseline.
Independent reviewers and subject matter experts validate that each product in the baseline is fully represented in the detailed design documentation.
policy_statements.actor_name: Independent reviewers and subject matter experts

policy_statements.source_text: This structured evaluation, often supported by checklists, compliance matrices, and risk assessments, provides confidence that the system is ready to enter testing.
Decision gate 6 is a review of the implementation, ensuring that the development and testing of the investment systems satisfy the desired functional requirements.

It accomplishes this by requiring evidence from unit tests, integration tests, and system-level verification reports that demonstrate compliance with business needs, functional requirements, and service level agreements.
Reviewers also assess user procedures, training materials, and operational documentation to confirm they meet stakeholder needs.
policy_statements.target: user procedures, training materials, and operational documentation

policy_statements.source_text: The gate uses test results, defect tracking, and performance metrics to verify that components adhere to physical constraints and operate as described in the user documentation.
This structured review process ensures that the system is not only built correctly but is also usable and supportable in practice.
Decision gate 7 determines whether system components achieve expected benefits.
It provides an evaluation of the investment’s development process.
It determines whether the investment is ready to go into O&M mode.
From the evaluation, there is a recommendation for continuing or modifying an investment.
Decision gate 8 determines whether system components are still providing their benefits at a reasonable cost, have reached the end of life, or will be disposed of (retired or decommissioned).
After an evaluation, there is a recommendation for terminating or disposing of, an investment.
Earned value management (EVM) is the integrated management system that USDA uses to coordinate the work scope, schedule, and cost goals of a program or contract.
USDA also uses it to objectively measure progress toward these goals.

Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must implement IT baseline management processes that meet certain minimum requirements that align with EVM best practices and the USDA’s enterprise governance process.

A rebaseline is the major realignment of the PMB to improve the correlation between the work plan and the baseline budget, scope, and schedule.
Rebaselining does not add or change the existing scope of work.
It merely changes how and when personnel may accomplish it within the constraints of the existing contract.
Personnel must not approve baseline changes for the sole purpose of offsetting variances.

Baseline changes are, however, acceptable for unexpected growth within the currently authorized work scope, rate changes, risk handling, and other program unknowns.
Rebaselining to offset variances erases important information useful for effective project management.
This is counter to the purpose of EVM.
However, if measuring and managing the current baseline is no longer viable, and EVM is no longer an effective tool for the management of the project, the project may be rebaselined.

The criteria for a rebaseline are as follows:
The schedule variance is equal to or greater than 10 percent; or
The budget variance is equal to or greater than 10 percent, or equal to or less than minus 10 percent; or
There is a scope change (any modification, adjustments, or additions to the project’s original goals, deliverables, or requirements).
Portfolio restructures are an integral aspect of strategic portfolio management (SPM).
They should be part of an ongoing process that focuses on aligning USDA’s IT resources with its strategic business goals.
As USDA continues to adopt agile development methods to respond to the rapidly changing business environment, there is also a need for agility at the strategic level.
Portfolio restructurings need to be able to quickly align budgets, resources, projects, and architecture roadmaps to new business strategies.
A portfolio restructuring enables an organization to neatly organize the information needed to optimize portfolios, improve agility, and set the pace for change.
Integrating portfolios enables impact analyses that reduce planning errors and improve synergies between the portfolios.
SPM needs to be a continuous process.
An organization needs to be able to continuously adapt to be resilient.
This means continuous analysis, decision-making, IT road mapping, planning, execution, monitoring, and finally returning full circle to analysis.
This needs to happen across all organizational hierarchies and units, from strategy to execution.
